heroText: Analyze hidden metadata, origin fingerprints and provenance. Clean what can be safely removed, then verify the output independently.
dropTitle: Drop files to break the metadata trail
dropText: JPEG, PNG, WebP, SVG, PDF, Office, ZIP/TAR, audio, MP4/MOV, HEIF/AVIF and more
limitText: Up to 20 files · 100 MB each · local processing
scanningSub: Parsing containers, provenance and origin indicators
chooseCleaning: Choose how far DataBreaker should go
safeDesc: Common privacy metadata, lowest compatibility risk.
everythingDesc: Aggressive removal of every known nonessential field that can be safely rewritten.
profileNote: Profiles never fabricate signatures or real-world origin claims.
footer: Privacy tooling should explain its limits.
policySafe: Safe Clean targets common privacy-sensitive metadata and keeps compatibility-oriented structural data such as color profiles.
policyDeep: Deep Clean additionally removes uncommon application metadata where the handler can do so without altering primary content.
policyEverything: Clean Everything removes every known nonessential metadata block the handler can safely rewrite. Cryptographic provenance may be removed and signatures may be invalidated. Content-like items are never silently deleted.
noRemaining: No known high/critical privacy findings remain after the independent rescan.
remainingText: Potentially identifying findings remain. Review them before sharing.
cleanUnsupported: Automatic cleaning is not available for this format; analysis remains available.
hostedModeText: Files are sent to this server for temporary processing and deleted after the operation. For maximum privacy, use the local or browser-only edition.
hostedLimitText: Hosted limit: files up to 4 MB · temporary server processing · no DataBreaker telemetry
browserModeText: Files are processed inside your browser with WebAssembly and are not uploaded to a DataBreaker backend.
browserLimitText: Browser-only processing · no server upload · practical limits depend on browser memory
